summary: New results start at the top with nothing selected, and ending a search puts the window back where it was. The first answer to a search whose words, scope, kind or Name/Contents changed clears the selection and puts the list and the icon view at the top (set_offset, not a deferred scroll); a search that only runs again keeps both. When a search begins, the window keeps the selected paths, the view, and the list's and the icon view's scroll offsets, and puts them back when the search ends without going elsewhere: both offsets always, plus a scroll to the selection in the gallery or in a view chosen during the search. Going to another place drops what was kept. Two things beyond the plan, each needed by a test: scroll_to does nothing in column view (it armed the list's handle, and the scroll fired on the next search's results), and location_changed puts both offsets at the top at once as well as at the next draw (a search sent together with a folder used to capture the folder before's offset). All of it is in src/finder/mod.rs.
changelog: Search results opened wherever the folder had been scrolled to, or at the end of a shorter list, with the best matches out of view, and they stayed scrolled when you typed on. Results now start at the top with nothing selected whenever the words, the scope, the kind, or Name and Contents change, so Down Arrow and Return in the search field go to the first result and not on from one selected earlier. A search that only runs again, as with Refresh, keeps its selection and stays where it was scrolled to. Ending a search with Escape or by emptying the search field puts the window back as it was before the search: the same items are selected, and the view is scrolled to the same place.
behaviour_changes: Results for other words start at the top of the list and of the icon view: the first letter after a scrolled folder, and typing on under scrolled results. Before, they opened at the folder's offset or at the end of a shorter list.

The same after a change of scope, kind, or Name/Contents. Tested: the scope bar's chips, the Kind menu, the Name and Contents chips. By reading only: the toolbar's Search Only in button and --here sent to a window that is already searching, which both go through set_scope.

The first answer to such a search clears the selection. Before, a result that still matched stayed selected. The status bar count, the path bar and the preview pane lose that item; the gallery moves to the first result; Down Arrow and Return in the search field, and Down Arrow in the files, go to the first result. Quick Look's window stays open and goes blank until something is selected again (probed: its Down Arrow then goes to the first result). A result selected between the change and its answer is dropped too.

A search that only runs again keeps its selection and scroll, as before. Tested: Refresh. Probed by the implementer: a quiet reload, the result limit, the hidden-files toggle. By reading: the retry while an index is built, file operations in the results, a filter turned on or off, the search settings; every one of them calls run_search, which does not set the flag.

Ending a search without going elsewhere puts the window back. The items selected before are selected again, by path, and the list and the icon view are both scrolled to the pixel offset they had, whichever of them is showing. Items gone since are skipped; a shorter list is scrolled as far as it goes. The gallery shows the item it was on. In column view the panes were already kept, and the window's own selection is back as well.

The ways a search ends that were run: Escape in the field, Escape twice in the files, Backspace to empty, New Folder (the new folder is selected, on screen, and takes the typed name), a Smart Folder in the folder the window is in (the place survives the Smart Folder's own search, also when it is run twice), going to the folder the window is already in, a letter typed and deleted before the answer, and the same from Recents and from the Trash. By reading only: the field's x button and Back with no history.
With the selection restored, the next Escape in the files clears it. In --pick mode that is one more Escape before the chooser is cancelled, when the search began with something selected (probed).

A view chosen during the search is, when the search ends, where that view was before the search (its top, if it had not been used in this folder), and scrolls to the selected item if there is one. Before the review it stayed at the results' scroll offset when nothing was selected.

A search no longer moves the view that isn't showing: list scrolled, Gallery, search, Escape, back to List finds the list where it was. Before the review the list was at its top afterwards, because the first answer puts both views there.

Column view: results no longer open at the row of an item selected earlier in the folder. Tested after Back. By reading only: after Up, a reveal, or a switch to Columns from another view with something selected, which armed the list's scroll the same way.

Going to another place moves the scroll positions at once as well as at the next draw. Nothing visible changes, except that a search sent together with a folder (fff gui, a second launch) ends at that folder's top. By reading only: if a listing arrives before any frame is drawn, the scroll to the item selected there starts from the top, not from the previous folder's offset.
A folder renamed or moved during a search is shown from its top when the search ends, as before; what was kept is dropped.

Manual: the second paragraph of Searching gains four sentences: results for other words start at the top with nothing selected; a search that runs again as it is keeps both; ending a search puts the window back; another view chosen during the search also scrolls to the selected item.
left_out: CHANGELOG.md is not edited, per the guide. The entry is in this record and in the commit message.
README.md is unchanged: it says nothing about this.
cargo clippy --features term was not run: src/term is untouched and nothing it calls changed (grepped src/term, src/macos.rs, src/win.rs, src/lib.rs, src/server, src/workspace.rs, examples).
Not compiled for macOS or Windows. src/finder/mod.rs has no cfg-gated code outside its tests, and the one new import (ScrollbarHandle) is used on every platform.

Several items selected before the search come back with the anchor on the first and the cursor on the last of them (Selection::select_items), not where they were. So the gallery, which shows the cursor's item, shows the last of them, and Shift+arrow goes on from there (probed: 003, 007, 010 selected with the cursor on 007 comes back with it on 010). One selected item is exact.

With a Nushell filter on, the place can come back only in part. When the search ends the folder's rows are filtered again, and until that has run they are the ones the search's filter kept. Items not among those aren't selected again, and the list can end a few rows off (probed with 200 items: two rows) or at its top.
Not captured: the list's sideways scroll, the gallery strip's offset (it follows the selection), and the column panes (they keep their selection and scroll through a search; probed).

In Recents, the Trash or sent results, switching between Columns and List during a search counts as choosing another view, though both list the items there, so the list then scrolls to the selected item when the search ends.

A result selected after the request changed but before its answer (a row clicked while a slow contents search runs for words typed since) is dropped when the answer arrives. That follows from the plan's reset at the answer.
No test that the retry while indexing leaves the list alone: the harness cannot stage a scan. It takes the same run_search path as Refresh, which is tested.
No 'before' picture of the column-view case, only 'after'.

review_fixes: return_to_before_search put the scroll positions back only when the view was the one the search began in, and never in the gallery. Two things followed. A view chosen during the search, with nothing selected in the folder, was left at the results' scroll offset, which is the brief's third problem in a corner: Icons, search, List, scroll the results, Escape showed the folder's list from item 124. And a search made in the gallery left the list at its top afterwards, because the first answer puts both views there: list scrolled, Gallery, search, Escape, List lost the list's place. Both offsets now always go back, and the gallery or a view chosen during the search scrolls to the selection as well, as set_view_mode does. Two tests added, both seen failing on the implementer's version: a_view_chosen_during_a_search_isnt_left_where_the_results_were and a_search_in_the_gallery_leaves_the_list_where_it_was.

ending_a_search_goes_back_to_where_recents_was_scrolled_to now selects the first item and scrolls it out of view before the search. After the fix above, its old form would have passed with the effective view captured instead of config.view_mode, which the comment at the capture warns against. Seen failing under that mutation.
docs/manual.md: the last of the four sentences reads 'If you chose another view during the search, it also scrolls to the selected item', to match the fix.
Commit message: its second paragraph says that both views are put back.
notes:
Checked. With the commit's src diff reverse-applied, 11 of the implementer's 16 tests failed; the four whose messages I read failed at the assertion that names the problem (the first result not on screen, the old result still selected). The other 5 are guards for what was already right and passed, as reported. The two tests added in review and the strengthened Recents test were each seen failing without their fix. I ran six mutations on the final code, one at a time, and each was caught by the test said to catch it and by no other in tests/basics.rs: every answer resetting (a_search_that_runs_again_keeps_its_place), location_changed keeping what was kept (a_folder_renamed_during_a_search_is_shown_from_its_top), an empty selection restored (a_gallery_chosen_during_a_search_still_shows_an_item), location_changed not moving the offsets at once (a_search_sent_along_with_a_folder_ends_at_that_folders_top), scroll_to arming the list in column view (new_results_start_at_the_top_in_column_view_too), and the reset done with scroll_to_item instead of set_offset (ending_a_search_goes_back_to_the_folders_place and the search sent with a folder). check.sh printed CHECK OK on the final commit: 501 passed in 16 test binaries, 3 of 3 known root-only failures. I looked at the window myself: results after the folder was scrolled to its end, the folder after Escape, and a view chosen during the search (the three review-*.png pictures).

The three ways this could most likely hurt someone, and what I found. (1) The list jumping to the top and losing its selection when the search did not change. The flag is set only in run_new_search, which set_query, set_scope, set_kind and set_search_contents call after their own no-change checks; all eleven other callers of run_search (Refresh, the index retry, the status poll, the settings, the hidden-files toggle, the filter, the quiet reload, batch rename, Return before the results) leave it alone; the first answer of the current generation takes it, and ending the search clears it, so it cannot outlive its search. (2) Something selected again that the user no longer expects, with a key like Cmd+Backspace then acting on it. Items come back only by exact path, only in the place the search began in (location_changed drops them), and only those selected before; the chooser needs one more Escape, nothing is chosen by itself. (3) An offset set at once being undone by a scroll that was still waiting, so results open at a stale row or the folder's place is lost a frame later. The reset and the restore use set_offset; the only waiting scrolls left are location_changed's two to the top and scroll_to on the view that is showing, which is drawn on the next frame. One window remains: End and the first letter of a search within one frame leave End's scroll waiting through the placeholders, and it fires on the results. Keys from a person are frames apart.

Doubts that remain, for the owner. (a) The selection is let go whenever the words, scope, kind or Name/Contents change, by design: the preview pane says No Selection, the gallery jumps to the first result, and a Quick Look window goes blank until something is selected. Before, an item that still matched stayed selected. (b) A row clicked while a slow contents search is still running for words typed since is deselected when that answer arrives, and the list goes to its top. (c) After a search, the folder's earlier selection is back, so the first Escape in the files clears it; in the chooser that is one more Escape before Cancel. (d) With a Nushell filter on, and with several items selected, the place comes back only approximately: see left_out. (e) The manual paragraph is long now; the sentences were kept in it, per the guide's rule on where documentation edits go.

For briefs still to come.
- search-start-no-flash: set_query's !was_searching branch captures the folder's place (selected paths, config.view_mode, both offsets) BEFORE drop_stale_results. If you keep the folder's items on screen until the first answer, capture at the same point, and note that the first answer clears the selection and puts both views at the top (new_search), so the folder's items may stay scrolled where they are until then. ending_a_search_goes_back_to_the_folders_place has a half for a search that never drew a list.
- live-search-results: quiet reruns must call run_search, not run_new_search, or the list jumps to the top and loses its selection on every update. a_search_that_runs_again_keeps_its_place pins Refresh.
- regex-content-search, smart-folder-save-and-leaks, recent-searches, kind-filter-single-list: a switch or a pick that changes what a search finds should go through run_new_search (it is private to mod.rs; make it pub(super) if you call it from another file). a_change_of_scope_kind_or_contents_starts_at_the_top_too clicks 'kind' and the menu item 'Document' and expects at least 200 results; update it if the Kind menu changes.
- back-forward-restore-search: location_changed drops before_search, and end_search runs return_to_before_search before the navigation. A search restored through set_query captures the place again, which right after a navigation is the top with nothing selected. If Back should return to scrolled results, that needs its own state.
- escape-ends-search: after Escape ends a search the folder's selection is back, so keys given to the files act on it, and Escape there clears it first.
- view-switch-keeps-selection: return_to_before_search calls scroll_to for the gallery and for a view chosen during the search, after putting both offsets back; your icon_reveal covers it if it lives in scroll_to. scroll_to now does nothing in column view.
- column-pane-selection-by-path: scroll_to's Columns arm is empty on purpose (the list's handle must not be armed there). The window's own selection is restored after a search in column view too.
- select-all-perf: the capture clones the selected paths once when a search begins; the restore is one pass over the rows with a HashSet. Selection::remap is untouched.
- quick-look-empty-state: new results now leave Quick Look with nothing selected every time the words change, not only when the item stopped matching.
- typo-fallback-near-miss, result-tie-break: new_results_start_at_the_top_of_the_list types 'item' and then 'txt' and expects at least 200 results for 'itemtxt'; the tests read the first result instead of naming it, so a change of order is fine.
- sorted-search-results: a re-sort of the results is not a new search; it keeps the selection and the scroll.
- restore-session-tabs: a tab opened with words captures an empty place (nothing selected, top), so Escape there shows the folder from its top.
- cancel-content-search's two search_abort lines are untouched.

Found, not fixed (there before this change).
- In column view, Back, Up and a reveal select the item in the window's selection, but the first pane shows nothing selected; Escape there clears only the window's selection.
- fffinder FILE --query words: the file to reveal is selected among the results if it is one of them, and is not selected in its folder when the search ends. The listing's selection is applied to whatever rows show when it arrives.
- With a Nushell filter on, a search that ends shows the folder's items through the search's filter result until the filter has run again.
- The list's sideways scroll is shared by a folder and its results and is never reset.
- tests/basics.rs renaming_in_place_works_in_every_view_but_the_gallery asserts !ui.exists("rename-field"), but that id has no test_support(), so the assertion cannot fail.
- Selection::remap costs selected x rows on every rebuild (select-all-perf).

Files of those kinds that other lanes made since are there (fix.patch, full.patch); I cannot tell whether any were lost. My own temporary files were in a folder of their own.
